channel.title: Economy
channel.description: Find the latest economic news, current events and headlines, as well as blogs and video from CNBC.com.

item.title: Jobless claims near the lowest since the 1960s as low-fire trend continues
item.description: Initial filings for unemployment insurance slipped to a seasonally adjusted 194,000.

item.title: Trump's approval rating on economy hits all-time low as midterm looms: CNBC survey
item.description: Eight out of 10 Americans now rate the economy as fair or poor, one of several findings in a CNBC poll that show why Republican candidates face uphill battles.

item.title: UK inflation jumps to 3.5% — cementing rate hike expectations
item.description: U.K. inflation rose by a hotter-than-expected 3.5% in the 12 months to September, driven by the surging cost of motor fuels.

item.title: Car buyers are demanding lower prices and better tech. Automakers must deliver both
item.description: Bain says tech leads purchase considerations in China while price remains No. 1 in the U.S. and Europe, as pressure mounts on Western carmakers.

item.title: Housing is flashing warning signs just as the Fed weighs more interest rate hikes
item.description: Housing data deteriorated further in September, according to separate reports Tuesday.

item.title: Women may be at greater risk of AI job losses. Telephone switch operators and PCs show why
item.description: The history of technological progress suggests that as AI spreads, the employment impact will hit women more than men.

item.title: India’s finance minister says market liquidity makes it easier for investors to exit
item.description: Sitharaman identified fuel, fertilizer and access to capital as risks for India’s economy in 2027.

item.title: U.S. budget deficit swells to almost $2 trillion for fiscal 2026, up 12% in a single year
item.description: The Treasury Department published the U.S. budget deficit for the 2026 fiscal year.

item.title: Analysis: Everyone expects the Fed to hold rates in October. Kevin Warsh could surprise us all
item.description: Investors expect the Fed to pause rate hikes in October, but Kevin Warsh's rejection of traditional communications practices and continued concern about inflation leave the decision uncertain.

item.title: Economists: Hot PPI shows Fed's work is not done
item.description: 'We see real risks the Fed will deliver another rate hike in two weeks' time,' one Fedwatcher warns

item.title: U.S. Treasury dismisses IMF debt warning and 'messy' forecasting
item.description: The exchange comes as U.S. debt exceeds $40 trillion and 10-year Treasury yields remain above 5%, intensifying scrutiny of the fiscal outlook.

item.title: Wholesale prices jumped 6.3% annually in September, biggest gain since 2022
item.description: September producer prices were expected to increase 0.6% month over month and 5.5% annually, according to the consensus estimate by Dow Jones.

item.title: Analysis: Why a $2 trillion deficit and 5% Treasury yields are becoming America's biggest economic challenge
item.description: Treasury yields above 5% are raising borrowing costs for households and the federal government, highlighting the challenge of financing $2 trillion deficits.

item.title: China indicates rare earths will keep flowing to EU, regardless of U.S. trade deal expiration
item.description: European trade commissioner Maroš Sefčovič met with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in Beijing last week.

item.title: UK economy grew 0.1% in August, beating expectations
item.description: The U.K. is grappling with a cost-of-living crisis sparked by sticky inflation and surging energy costs.

item.title: How high inflation became a 'fact of life' in the U.S.
item.description: U.S. inflation has stayed elevated for years, raising concern at the Federal Reserve that consumers may come to expect stubbornly high prices.

item.title: Consumer prices rose 3.7% annually in September as gas prices skyrocket
item.description: The consumer price index was expected to increase 0.6% in September on a monthly basis and 3.6% from a year ago, according to the Dow Jones consensus forecast.

item.title: 'Godzilla El Niño' is wreaking havoc with Philippine central bank's inflation forecasts
item.description: The Philippine central bank is running policy scenarios for a severe El Niño on top of the oil shock, with inflation at a three-year high.

item.title: The latest inflation data is expected to show price increases are accelerating
item.description: Economists expect the consumer price index for September to rise 0.6% on the month and 3.6% year over year.

item.title: In charts: How one of the world's biggest economies got trapped by debt
item.description: France opens debate on its 2027 budget as high deficits, rising debt and student protests intensify pressure on lawmakers.

item.title: IMF warns bond yields could see a 'disorderly' spike as debt, inflation risks worsen
item.description: The IMF says risks in the government bond market have worsened and that yields could jump sharply and disorderly.

item.title: IMF sees milder global slowdown as AI boom offsets war hit — warns resilience is nearing limits
item.description: The IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, warning that resilience is tested by energy constraints and looming fiscal risks.

item.title: India’s retail inflation jumps to 5.54% in September, above estimates
item.description: India inflations jumps for the 11-straight month, raising prospects of a further interest rate hike

item.title: Nobel prize in economics awarded to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford
item.description: The U.S. economists were awarded for work that underpins the models used by central banks and governments to stabilize the economy.

item.title: World Bank jobs council urges 'crisis-era' employment support measures as IMF warns of AI ‘tsunami’
item.description: IMF Chief Kristalina Georgieva warned AI is hitting the global labor market like a “slow-moving tsunami,” with young workers entering the job market the most exposed.

item.title: Americans' debt problems are flashing a warning not seen since the Great Recession
item.description: Researchers found that while wealth disparities narrowed somewhat, the ability to meet debt payments deteriorated significantly.

item.title: Treasury's Bessent hires Trump's controversial former Fed board pick, Judy Shelton, as advisor
item.description: Shelton's controversial economic ideas led the Senate to block her nomination to the Fed. Now she's going to be a counselor to the Treasury secretary.

item.title: Inflation on many everyday items was entirely due to tariffs, NY Fed says
item.description: Tariffs added 2.9 percentage points to inflation in 67 categories of goods by February 2026, researchers at the New York Federal Reserve found.

item.title: Inflation fears on the rise as one-year outlook in Fed survey hits highest level since May 2023
item.description: The Survey of Consumer Expectations indicated that the median outlook for inflation over the next 12 months rose to 3.9%.

item.title: ICE came to town and left behind weakened economies
item.description: Research links ICE enforcement surges to lasting declines in local spending, foot traffic and jobs. In Minneapolis, businesses are still recovering.
